summary: Tested new Purchases / PDF invoice import feature end-to-end. Backend: 8/8 pytest cases passed covering PDF parse (Alfa+Grimco), create-with-upsert (created + updated + stock-added), list+filter, CSV export, delete, RBAC. Frontend: full flow verified — admin login, navigate to Purchases, open dialog, upload Alfa PDF, parse into editable draft (supplier=Alfa Paper, invoice=177613, 7 line rows, paper module chip preselected), save purchase, verify row appears, supplier filter narrows results, CSV export downloads purchases.csv, Materials page shows Alfa Paper items. Post-test cleanup completed (deleted test purchase + 7 Alfa materials I created).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~2195 lines; consider splitting into modular routers (purchases, materials, finance) — approaching the 700-line advisory limit x3.
parse_invoice_with_llm has no timeout guard; if EMERGENT_LLM_KEY expires or gpt-4o is slow, endpoint just 502s — could add explicit asyncio.wait_for + friendlier error.
DELETE /api/purchases/{pid} returns {ok:true} regardless of whether the id existed (no 404 for missing). Minor.
seed_data_creation: None left. Created 2 test purchases + 7 Alfa Paper materials during pytest and UI test; all deleted at teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature is production-ready. test_purchases.py can be re-run as regression. Parse endpoint calls gpt-4o (~4-8s), so keep timeouts >=60s. UI file upload works via hidden <input type='file' data-testid='purchase-file-input'> — use set_input_files, not clicking dropzone.
